tools.name: add_leads_to_campaign
tools.description: Move leads this account owns into a campaign this account owns. Updates membership only — sends nothing. If the target campaign was already reviewed, its approval token becomes unusable (launch recounts recipients), so a fresh review_campaign_readiness is required before launching.

tools.name: analyze_lead_source
tools.description: Summarise the leads in an account or one campaign: how many exist, how many can actually be contacted, how many opted out, and how they break down by status and source. Read-only — sends nothing and changes nothing. Start here when the operator asks what they have to work with.

tools.name: create_campaign_draft
tools.description: Create a campaign in draft status with its opening SMS. THIS SENDS NOTHING — a draft cannot deliver a message. It exists so a human can read the exact wording and audience before deciding. The message is rejected if it implies a prior relationship or manufactures urgency. After this, call review_cam

tools.name: create_lead
tools.description: Add a single lead to a campaign this account owns. Requires campaign_id plus at least a phone or an email; deduplicates against the account's existing leads by contact detail. Writes a record only — sends nothing, to nobody, ever.

tools.name: find_lead
tools.description: Search this account's leads by phone number, email address, or name. Phone matching tolerates formatting differences. Returns masked contact details plus lead ids. Read-only — sends nothing and changes nothing.

tools.name: get_campaign_status
tools.description: Report what a campaign has actually done: leads, messages delivered, replies, opt-outs, meetings scheduled, and threads waiting on a human. Omit campaign_id to list every campaign in the account. Read-only. The response includes caveats about which numbers may lag — read them before telling the oper

tools.name: get_interested_leads
tools.description: List leads whose replies were classified as positive or as asking a question, newest first, with the reply text. The classifier is keyword and sentiment based, NOT a language model — the response says so explicitly, and the reply text is included so you can judge for yourself. Read-only.

tools.name: launch_approved_campaign
tools.description: SENDS REAL MESSAGES TO REAL PEOPLE. This is irreversible and costs credits. It requires an approval_token from review_campaign_readiness AND the confirmation phrase that review returned, which the HUMAN OPERATOR must give you explicitly. Never generate the confirmation yourself, never infer approval

tools.name: list_from_addresses
tools.description: The verified email sender identities (from-addresses) this account can send campaigns from. Read-only; sends nothing. Use before an email-channel readiness review to pick the right sender.

tools.name: list_leads
tools.description: Page through this account's leads, optionally filtered by campaign and status. Read-only — sends nothing and changes nothing.

tools.name: pause_campaign
tools.description: Stop a campaign from sending anything further. Queued messages that have not yet gone out are skipped; anything already handed to the carrier cannot be recalled. Safe to call when unsure — pausing is reversible and errs toward not contacting people.

tools.name: recommend_followup_campaign
tools.description: Propose how to follow up, based on which leads have never been contacted, were contacted without replying, or already replied. Returns segments with counts and a suggested approach for each. Read-only — this is a proposal to discuss with the operator, not a plan that has been put into effect.

tools.name: review_campaign_readiness
tools.description: Pre-flight a campaign: how many people would be contacted, on which channels, what it would cost, and which checks pass, warn or fail. SENDS NOTHING. If everything passes, it returns a short-lived approval token and a confirmation phrase — both of which a human operator must authorise before launch_

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: create_campaign_draft, find_lead, get_campaign_status, list_from_addresses · Private data: add_leads_to_campaign, create_lead, find_lead, review_campaign_readiness · Public sink: create_campaign_draft, create_lead, find_lead, list_from_addresses · Destructive: review_campaign_readiness.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: create_campaign_draft, find_lead, get_campaign_status, list_from_addresses · Private data: add_leads_to_campaign, create_lead, find_lead, review_campaign_readiness · Public sink: create_campaign_draft, create_lead, find_lead, list_from_addresses · Destructive: review_campaign_readiness

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
